# Glossary for boxed terminals

**Verifier** — any command the instructions treat as authoritative for pass or fail.

**Surface** — the filesystem and processes you can reach from the current shell; if
listings disagree with the brief, your surface is wrong before the code is wrong.

**Burst** — a set of tool calls that can all run without waiting on unknown paths; batch
them together.

**Lane** — a single file or coherent directory tree you edit without overlapping unrelated
writes on the same path.

**Smoke** — the smallest command that exercises the last change (compile one file, run one
test node, print one config).

**Fence** — boundaries the brief draws; outside the fence is not your job this episode.

**Handoff** — one durable sentence future you can trust; not a transcript.

## Application

Start by making the verifier line concrete. Freeze the fence. Run bursts for discovery,
then one lane at a time with a smoke between lanes. When the verifier passes, write a
handoff only if you learned a pattern, not a diary entry.

If a command fails twice with the same shape, change the diagnosis—not the decoration on
the same command.
